## Origin

reflect light mode, lens "Friction", from #2356,#2357,#2358,#2359

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow`'s Step 3 (Pipeline Config Manifesto) is documented as unconditional — it
"runs after pre-flight passes" regardless of which steps are in the resolved step list, and
writes `config.yml` + initializes `decisions.md`'s config snapshot header before Step 4 begins.

On this run (`2026-09-14T071315-record-2356`, a dispatch-minted bundle for #2356/#2357/#2358/#2359),
the dispatching session's first `/flow` call ran `build,test` against this run directory — its
`decisions.md` shows `## /build` and `## /test` sections with real entries (materialize, test
pass, PR-early lifecycle) — but no `config.yml` was ever written, and `decisions.md` carries no
manifesto log line at all. When this second call resumed the same run directory for
`review,polish,wrap-up`, `config.yml` was missing entirely (confirmed via `ls`/`test -f`), forcing
this call to reconstruct the 13 lever values by hand from a same-day sibling bundle
(#2230/#2354/#2355, archived run `2026-09-13T224009-record-2230-2354-2355`) rather than reading
them back from the run's own first-call Manifesto write.

## Deliverables

- Investigate why Step 3 did not execute (or executed but failed to persist `config.yml`) on a
  `/flow {target} build,test` invocation against a dispatch-minted, `config.yml`-less run
  directory — check whether Step 3's adoption branch (`steps-and-gates.md`'s "Adopting an
  inherited run directory") has a gap for the `build,test`-only step-list shape specifically,
  versus the full default step list.
- Either fix the gap so every `/flow` call against a fresh run directory writes `config.yml`
  before Step 4 runs, or (if this is intentional deferred-Manifesto behavior for a narrow step
  list) document that a later resuming call must re-derive/re-run Step 3 itself, rather than
  silently finding `config.yml` absent with no signal of why.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `/flow {target} build,test` call against a freshly dispatch-minted run directory (no
      pre-existing `config.yml`) leaves `config.yml` present and populated with the 13 canonical
      levers by the time the call returns.
- [ ] If the investigation finds this was actually correct behavior for some other reason, this
      record closes with that reasoning documented instead of a code change.

## Evidence

`decisions.md`'s `## /build`/`## /test` sections (real entries, no manifesto line) versus
`config.yml` absent from the run directory at the start of this second `/flow ... review,polish,wrap-up`
call; `test -f "$RUN_DIR/config.yml"` → `MISSING`, confirmed before this call wrote one itself.

## Cost this session

~10 minutes: reading manifesto.md's full lever-computation procedure, finding and cross-checking
the sibling bundle's archived config.yml as a same-day precedent, and manually composing +
writing the batch `set-config.js` call, instead of the value being readable off the run's own
first-call state.

## Decision-log reference

AUTO 09:36:46 — manifesto: config.yml was missing on resume (this call's step list is
review,polish,wrap-up — the first call's build/test steps ran without ever writing it); wrote it
now, folding values from the sibling reconcile-residue bundle run (#2230,#2354,#2355, archived
2026-09-14T01:01, same policy.yml/autonomy=unattended, merged via PR #2387)...

## Current State

During a scheduled Routine firing of `/claude-tweaks:dispatch next` in a gh-absent cloud sandbox, the queue pull correctly fell back to a persisted queue-order cache match (avoiding a fresh gh-based pull), but per `skills/dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s documented gap, `dispatch-open-pr-excluded.json` was written as `{}` unconditionally since there's no confirmed MCP mapping for `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js`'s batched `closedByPullRequestsReferences` query. This let record #1841 through dispatch's Step 3 ranking and Step 5 dispatch despite already having an open draft PR (#2382, "Resolve acceptance-labeling parent via GraphQL (#1841)") with all four phases (build/test/review/wrap-up) checked complete, parked awaiting a human at wrap-up.

The dispatched `/claude-tweaks:flow #1841 build,test` Task call safely stopped at Step 2.8's claim-contest check (the record's live claim, held by a different, non-expired run, correctly blocked a second claim) and deduplicated against an existing self-report (#2394) from an earlier firing that hit the identical contest ~2 hours prior. No data was lost and no destructive git action occurred — the dispatching session's own newly-created worktree (also coincidentally named `worktree-record-1841`, since `EnterWorktree`'s naming keyed off the same record number) held zero commits beyond `origin/main`'s tip and was safely discarded after an ancestry check.

So the claim-contest safety net worked as designed, but it's a slower, more expensive catch than the open-PR exclusion this record's own `mcp-transport.md` gap left disabled — the record was picked at all, a worktree was minted, project setup plus a full baseline `npm test` ran (~150s), and a Task-tool subagent dispatch was spent, all for a record dispatch's own queue pull should have excluded up front had the MCP mapping existed.

## Deliverables

- A confirmed MCP mapping (or a documented reason none is feasible) for `bin/resolve-linked-prs.js`'s batched `closedByPullRequestsReferences` query across a candidate set, following the same verification bar `mcp-transport.md`'s other confirmed mappings cite (a live cloud Routine run, per the dispatch MCP bridge plan's Task 2 precedent).
- Update `skills/dispatch/mcp-transport.md`'s "Step 2 — open-linked-PR exclusion (#1224)" section once bridged, removing the "not yet bridged" language.
- Optionally: since the claim-contest self-report path already surfaces the open-PR fact (issue #2382's number) once discovered mid-flight, consider whether `_shared/headless-self-report.md`'s claim-contest report could name the open PR directly when one exists, saving a future firing's dispatching session the same PR lookup this incident required by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On the MCP transport (`gh` absent), a record with an open, unmerged, closing PR is excluded from `dispatch-groups.json` before ranking, matching the `gh`-transport's existing behavior — not just caught later by the claim-contest safety net.
- `npm test` passes.

Filed by a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch --budget 1` scheduled Routine firing, 2026-09-14, after directly observing this documented gap cause a real (safely-contained) mis-dispatch of #1841 against open PR #2382.

Origin: wrap-up of #1841
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s `acceptance-labeling` check (registered via `registerCheck('acceptance-labeling', ...)`) unconditionally expects a resolved, non-parent-linked issue to carry `demo:pending` plus a Confirmed comment/brief, rendering `fail` when it's absent. `wrap-up/verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate (`#367`, `bin/lib/issues/oversight-floor.js`'s `exceedsOversightFloor`) legitimately skips Steps 1-4 (no `demo:pending` bootstrap, no brief) for a record whose `risk`/`size` facets don't clear the project's configured `risk-floor`/`size-floor` — e.g. a `risk:low`/`size:low` record under a run resolving `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high`. `engine-verify.js` has no knowledge of this exemption, so `wrap-up-engine.js verify` renders `acceptance-labeling` as `fail` and exits 3 for every such record, withholding the closure line even though the record's labeling is exactly as `verification-brief.md` intends.

Observed live during #1841's own wrap-up: the record carries `risk:low`/`size:low`, the resolved run policy set `risk-floor: high`/`size-floor: high`, `exceedsOversightFloor` correctly returned `exceeds: false`, Steps 1-4 were correctly skipped — and `verify`'s `acceptance-labeling` row then rendered `fail — #1841: missing demo:pending label`, a false negative on a check that was never supposed to run for this record.

## Deliverables

- `acceptance-labeling`'s check needs a way to know a record was Oversight-floor-exempted, so it can render `skip (oversight floor not cleared)` instead of `fail` for that record — likely by having `verification-brief.md`'s Oversight-floor gate write the outcome into `verify-expectations.json` (a new field, e.g. `oversightExempt: [n1, n2]`) the same way `memory`/`upstream` are already written there, and having `engine-verify.js` read it before checking for `demo:pending`.
- Extend `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.test.js`: an issue listed in `verify-expectations.json`'s new exemption field renders `acceptance-labeling` as `skip`, never `fail`, even with no `demo:pending` label present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record whose Oversight-floor gate resolved `exceeds: false` (recorded in `verify-expectations.json`) renders `acceptance-labeling` as `skip`, and does not trip `verify`'s exit-3 gate on that account alone.
- A record that genuinely should carry `demo:pending` but doesn't still renders `fail` as today — the fix narrows the false-positive population, it does not loosen the check generally.
- `npm test` passes.

Origin: /claude-tweaks:feedback session-evaluation (self-assessment, degraded from a failed Frontier judge dispatch), self-referential run (this repo's own origin is thomasholknielsen/claude-tweaks) — routed to a normal backlog record per Step 3 rather than filed as upstream feedback.

## Current State

Worktrees created via the harness-native `EnterWorktree` tool (rather than `plugin/skills/dispatch/`'s own `record-worktree` CLI) never get their worktree/branch association written into that run's `run-state.json`. Downstream, `teardown-run`/`archive-run` (`plugin/bin/hooks.js`) can't find the association and report "no worktree recorded" instead of tearing the worktree down automatically. In one session this recurred across 7 separate worktrees, each requiring a manual `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proof + `git worktree remove --force` + `git branch -D` + `gh api -X DELETE .../refs/heads/{branch}` sequence in place of one CLI call — roughly 14 extra manual commands that a working association would have made unnecessary. A related recovery-quality symptom from the same gap: a prior session's main checkout was found 256 commits behind `origin/main` while still holding uncommitted archival bookkeeping from an earlier `/tidy` run — state left behind with no automatic reconciliation path, blocking a later session's own `archive-run` calls until manually resolved via a scratch-worktree PR.

Related, narrower observation from the same evaluation: the ledger's canonical Create location (`docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-{feature}-ledger.md`, per `_shared/ledger-format.md`) requires a worktree write under `worktree-always`, but `residue-sweep.md` explicitly expects a standalone (no-worktree) wrap-up run to be able to create one "so the ledger's own resolve gate has something to enforce on a standalone run." In practice a standalone run has no lightweight path to satisfy this — creating a ledger file for a single non-blocking item means a full worktree-commit-push-PR-merge cycle for a file that gets deleted moments later once resolved.

## Deliverables

1. Either make `EnterWorktree` call `record-worktree` itself when the harness detects a claude-tweaks-managed repo, or make `teardown-run`/`archive-run` fall back to `git worktree list`/branch-name matching when `run-state.json` carries no worktree field.
2. Let a standalone, no-worktree wrap-up log ledger items to a location that doesn't require a worktree write — e.g. `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/` (already commit-exempt under `worktree-always` and already the run's own audit-trail home) instead of `docs/plans/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree entered via `EnterWorktree` during a dispatch/wrap-up run is torn down by `teardown-run`/`archive-run` without a "no worktree recorded" failure and without any manual `git worktree remove`/`git branch -D`/`gh api DELETE` fallback.
- A standalone wrap-up run with at least one ledger item can create, resolve, and delete its ledger without needing a worktree, a commit, or a PR.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js`'s `readState` derives push status from the configured upstream only: it runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`, and when that fails it sets `upstream: null` and `pushed: false` — the comment reads "Absent an upstream there is nowhere for the work to have gone, so it is unpushed". `bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` then prints `{head} — {commits}, UNPUSHED (no upstream)`, and `bin/wrap-up-state.js` uses `state.upstream` to pick which reflog to read. That premise is false for every `pr-first` run: `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s Step 2 and `_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push use `git push origin {branch}` with no `-u`, so `@{u}` stays unset (or, since #1860, points at the branch-off point `origin/main` when the worktree was created with `-b {branch} origin/main`) while `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` is up to date after every push. The State block that `wrap-up/summary-template.md` says to render verbatim therefore claims UNPUSHED for work that origin already holds, and the reporter had to run `git branch --set-upstream-to` by hand to get a truthful line.

The ref the helper needs is already local: `git push origin {branch}` updates `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` in the pushing checkout, so no fetch is required to judge a push this run made; a fetch would only matter for pushes made elsewhere, which the wrap-up State block is not asked to cover.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `readState` gains a remote-ref fallback: when `@{u}` is unset, or resolves to a ref other than `origin/{branch}`, it checks `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options refs/remotes/origin/{branch}`; when that ref exists, `ahead`/`behind` are computed with `rev-list --left-right --count refs/remotes/origin/{branch}...HEAD` and `pushed` follows the same `ahead === 0` rule. The result carries a new `remoteRef` field (`'origin/{branch}'` or `null`) and a `pushedVia: 'upstream' | 'remote-ref' | null` field; `upstream` keeps reporting the configured `@{u}` (or `null`) unchanged.
- [ ] `render.js` distinguishes the three shapes: `pushed (origin/{branch}; no upstream configured)` when `pushedVia === 'remote-ref'`; the existing `pushed`/`UNPUSHED ({upstream})` lines when `pushedVia === 'upstream'`; `UNPUSHED (no upstream, origin/{branch} absent)` when neither ref exists. The unknown case (`pushed === null`) keeps its current wording.
- [ ] `bin/wrap-up-state.js`'s reflog read uses `state.remoteRef` when `state.upstream` is null, so the concatenated-reflog logic sees the remote-tracking ref's updates too.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js` (fake-runner style, beside the three existing `pushed` cases): no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 0 → `pushed: true`, `pushedVia: 'remote-ref'`; no upstream + remote ref present + ahead 2 → `pushed: false`; no upstream + no remote ref → `pushed: false`, `remoteRef: null`; inherited upstream (`origin/main`) + remote ref present → judged by the remote ref, not `@{u}`; existing cases unchanged. `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` pins the three rendered lines.
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/` line (the family-1 sentence that says `state.js` reads branch/upstream/ahead-behind/pushed facts) names the remote-ref fallback in one clause.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On a branch pushed with `git push origin {branch}` and no upstream configured, `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` renders a `pushed` line naming `origin/{branch}`; after one more local commit it renders `UNPUSHED` with the ahead count.
2. On a branch whose `@{u}` is the inherited `origin/main` (the #1860 shape) but whose `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` matches HEAD, the line reads pushed, not `UNPUSHED (origin/main)`.
3. A branch that was never pushed still renders UNPUSHED, and a failed `rev-list` read under either ref still yields `pushed: null` (unknown), never a definite false.
4. All existing `state.test.js` and `render.test.js` cases pass unmodified; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Helper-side fallback rather than `-u` on the lifecycle's first push: the fallback fixes the State block for branches pushed by any tool (the record's own second point), needs no change to the three skill files that spell the push command, and does not interact with `hasNoUpstreamYet` in `pre-tool-use.js`, which since #1860 already reads `@{u}` vs `origin/{branch}` and would need re-verification if the lifecycle started setting upstreams. The `--end-of-options` separator before the ref follows the repo's `git` argument rule (#1686's citation).

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/state.js` — `readState` (the `@{u}` read, `ahead`/`behind`, the `pushed` rule and its comment).
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/render.js` — the `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` line and its siblings.
- `plugin/bin/wrap-up-state.js` — `state.upstream` reflog selection.
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/state.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/render.test.js` — fake-runner fixtures.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`, `plugin/skills/_shared/git-discipline.md` — read-only: the push form that leaves `@{u}` unset.

## Gotchas
- `git branch --show-current` returns empty on a detached HEAD; the fallback must skip the remote-ref probe when `branch` is null, keeping today's detached-HEAD output.
- A remote named anything other than `origin` is out of scope; the lifecycle pushes to `origin` by contract (`_shared/integration-branch.md`), so hard-code it and say so in the comment rather than parsing `branch.{name}.remote`.
- The ordering rule stays: `pushed` is judged against whichever ref was chosen, never against both; a configured upstream that equals `origin/{branch}` takes precedence and the fallback is not consulted.
- `pushedVia` is additive on the JSON shape `--json` emits (#1930); no existing consumer reads the new field, so the shape change is backward compatible.

## Original request
**Summary:** `wrap-up-state.js --since <base>` rendered `Branch <branch> — 12 commits, UNPUSHED (no upstream)` for a branch whose every commit was already on `origin` (the phase-exit push had just printed `<old>..<new> <branch> -> <branch>`). The pr-first lifecycle pushes with `git push origin {branch}` — never `-u` — so `@{u}` is unset on every pr-first run and the helper's "pushed" judgment is wrong for exactly the runs whose State block the wrap-up summary is told to render verbatim.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/wrap-up-state.js` (push-status derivation), with `skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 2 / `skills/_shared/git-discipline.md`'s phase-exit push as the reason `@{u}` is never set

**Cost this session:** one manual `git branch --set-upstream-to` to make the State block truthful, plus a Verdict line that had to be written from the push output instead of the helper — the opposite of what `summary-template.md` asks for ("never assert it landed from memory").

**Repro steps:**
1. Run any pr-first pipeline (draft PR opened at run start; phases push with `git push origin {branch}`).
2. At wrap-up, run `node bin/wrap-up-state.js --since <merge-base>`.
3. Observe `UNPUSHED (no upstream)` while `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/{branch}` returns the current HEAD sha.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: when `@{u}` is unset, the helper falls back to `refs/remotes/origin/{branch}` (after the fetch it already does, or via `git ls-remote`) and reports pushed/unpushed from that; or the pr-early lifecycle's first push sets the upstream (`-u`) so `@{u}` is meaningful for the rest of the run.
Actual: the helper reports UNPUSHED whenever no upstream is configured, regardless of what origin holds.

**Definition:** Clear — either fix (helper fallback or `-u` on the first push) makes the State block correct; the helper-side fallback also covers branches pushed by tools that never set upstream.

**Plugin version:** 6.114.1

Surface: infra

## Current State
`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` composes the shared draft PR body once, at run start (Step 3), including the phase checklist between the `phases-start`/`phases-end` markers. Two rules there decide whether a `polish` row exists:

1. Creation: "Omit a `polish` row when the record's `surface:` is `backend` (polish never runs)". In a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` run the PR is opened once, before spec 1's build, so "the record" is spec 1 and the rule never looks at specs 2..N.
2. Skip: "a skipped phase's row is removed at that phase's own would-be exit rather than predicted at creation". In a multi-spec run, spec 1's would-be polish exit removes the row even when spec 2 is frontend and will run polish minutes later.

`flow/multispec-pr-checklist.md` (#921) makes the rows cumulative and run-level (never reset per spec) but says nothing about rows that were never created or were removed by an earlier spec's skip. Net effect, as observed on a five-spec batch at 6.111.0 with a backend spec first: specs 2-4 ran real polish and the PR's checklist shows no polish row at all; the evidence lives only in each spec's `decisions.md` and `manifest.yml`.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Creation rule widened in `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` Step 3: omit the `polish` row only when **every** record in the run has `surface: backend` — for a multi-spec run, read the batch's surfaces from the parent `manifest.yml`'s `specs[]` (the same list Step 3 already walks to emit one `Fixes #{m}` line per record); a single-record run keeps the current single-surface rule unchanged. `flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s phase-exit paragraph restates the creation rule ("omitted at PR creation only for a backend `surface:`") and is updated to the every-record wording in the same change.
- [ ] Skip rule scoped in the same file's Phase-checklist update section: in a multi-spec run, a spec's would-be polish exit never removes the row; the row stays `- [ ] polish` until some spec's real polish exit flips it, or the Pre-merge title/description refresh removes a still-unchecked `polish` row when no spec in the run ran polish. Single-record runs keep the current would-be-exit removal.
- [ ] `flow/multispec-pr-checklist.md`: one paragraph stating the run-level polish-row rule (present when any spec can run polish; checked by the first spec that does; removed at pre-merge only if none did), pointing at the two `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` rules above.
- [ ] `flow/multi-spec.md`'s "PR phase-checklist convention" section gains one sentence naming the polish-row rule.
- [ ] Conformance assertions in `tests/pr-early-run-lifecycle.test.js`: the creation rule names the every-record condition and `manifest.yml`'s `specs[]`; the skip rule names the multi-spec deferral to the pre-merge refresh; `multispec-pr-checklist.md` carries the polish-row paragraph.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. For a multi-spec run whose first spec is backend and any later spec is frontend, the Step 3 template as documented yields a `- [ ] polish` row on the shared PR at creation.
2. For a multi-spec run whose every spec is backend, the row is omitted at creation exactly as today.
3. A backend spec's would-be polish exit in a multi-spec run leaves the row in place; a frontend spec's polish exit flips it to `- [x] polish`; the pre-merge refresh removes only a row still unchecked at that point.
4. Single-record runs: creation and skip behavior byte-identical to today's prose.
5. The conformance suite pins each of the three prose changes; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Prose-only change across three skill files plus test pins; no `bin/` code reads or writes the polish row (the checklist update is the compose-then-write-once `gh pr edit` procedure each phase skill performs). The creation rule's data source already exists at Step 3 (the `Fixes` enumeration walks `manifest.yml`'s `specs[].id`); extend that walk to `specs[]`'s surface facet, read per `flow/materialize.md`'s Resolution (the `surface:` lift rule `multi-spec.md` Step 3 pre-flight already applies), so the rule needs no new lookup. The pre-merge refresh (its step 2 re-runs the checklist update unconditionally) is the natural place for the deferred removal, since it is the last write before undraft.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — Step 3 template and the "Omit a `polish` row" rule; Phase-checklist update section's skipped-phase sentence; "Multi-spec runs share one PR" paragraph; Pre-merge title/description refresh step 2.
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-pr-checklist.md` — cumulative-rows rationale; add the polish-row paragraph.
- `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md` — "PR phase-checklist convention (shared PR)" section.
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` — the polish phase-exit paragraph that restates the creation rule.
- `tests/pr-early-run-lifecycle.test.js` — existing prose pins for the checklist template.

## Gotchas
- `no-polish` on the step list is run-wide and still removes the row at the would-be exit (single-record) or at pre-merge (multi-spec); the rule change is about surface, not about the explicit escape hatch.
- Dispatch bundles (`dispatch/SKILL.md` file-overlap groups) share the same Step 3 template and the same `specs[]` walk, so the every-record condition applies to them too; say so in the Step 3 prose rather than leaving bundles to the single-record rule.
- The `surface:` facet can be absent on a record; the creation rule must count an absent surface as "can run polish" (only an explicit `backend` omits), because the real polish decision is made at runtime by `flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s decision tree and detection layer 2 — creation must never pre-empt it toward omission.
- Do not add a per-spec axis to the checklist; #921 declined it deliberately and `manifest.yml`'s `specs[].phase` remains the per-spec source.

## Original request
**Summary:** A multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` batch's shared PR checklist is seeded once at PR creation from the *first* spec's surface, so when that first spec is backend (correctly omitting the polish row per the plugin's own rule) but a *later* spec in the same batch is frontend and genuinely runs polish, the PR checklist has no row to reflect that polish ever happened.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s phase-checklist template, as used by `/claude-tweaks:flow`'s multi-spec mode

**Use case:** A 5-spec multi-spec `/flow` batch where spec 1 is backend (`Surface: backend`) and specs 2-4 are frontend (`Surface: web`, `Design-intent: quiet`). The shared PR is opened at spec 1's build step; its phase checklist is seeded from spec 1's surface and correctly omits the polish row (backend specs skip polish). Specs 2-4 are genuinely frontend and each runs a real polish phase — design-intent-driven fixes get applied and logged to each spec's own `decisions.md`/`manifest.yml` — but the shared PR's checklist template has no per-spec-id axis, so there's no row anywhere on the PR itself showing that polish ran, or what it found. The only place this is visible is inside each spec's own run-directory audit trail, not the PR a reviewer would actually look at.

**Definition:** Clear — the fix is a well-defined widening of the template (e.g. a single run-level polish row that appears once any spec in the batch needs it, rather than deriving polish applicability from only the first spec), not an open design question.

**Plugin version:** 6.111.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review. Two independently-merged PRs each shipped their
own Jaccard-similarity tokenizer and threshold constant, with no shared source and no test
importing either exported constant — so a change to one can silently invalidate the other's
tests without either noticing:

- `plugin/bin/lib/coordination.js` (confirmed, line 17, #1980): `SUBSTANCE_SIMILARITY_MIN = 0.4`
  + `SUBSTANCE_STOP_WORDS` (line 22).
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js` (confirmed, line 24, #1944):
  `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5` + `STOP_WORDS` (line 30).

`tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js:66` hardcodes "0.5" in a test name/reasoning
(`'title similarity below the default 0.5 threshold does not fire'`) instead of importing the
real constant.

## Deliverables

- Decide whether these two similarity checks are conceptually the same primitive (in which case
  consolidate into one shared tokenizer/threshold module both import) or genuinely distinct
  enough to justify separate constants (in which case document why, and have each test import
  its own module's real constant instead of hardcoding the value).
- Update `near-duplicate.test.js` to import `DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` rather than
  hardcoding 0.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

No test hardcodes either threshold as a bare numeric literal; both are imported from their
source module.

## Technical Approach

Read both modules' full similarity-scoring logic (`coordination.js`'s substance-similarity check
and `near-duplicate.js`'s title-similarity check) to judge whether they're the same primitive
applied to different inputs (substance text vs. titles) or genuinely distinct enough to warrant
separate stop-word lists and thresholds — this is the actual judgment call the Deliverables ask
for, not a mechanical decision this shaping pass can make without reading both algorithms'
full bodies. If consolidating: extract a shared tokenizer/stop-word/threshold module both import,
preserving each call site's own threshold value unless the investigation finds a reason to unify
those too. If keeping them separate: add a one-line comment at each constant's definition site
stating why the two are conceptually distinct, and fix the test regardless — the test-hardcoding
fix (Deliverable 2) applies either way. Update `near-duplicate.test.js:66` to import
`DEFAULT_TITLE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` and interpolate it into the test name/assertion instead of
the bare literal `0.5`.

  possible consolidation target
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/near-duplicate.test.js` (line 66) — fix the hardcoded `0.5`

## Gotchas

- Per a standing memory in this codebase, similarity scores are normalization-sensitive —
  consolidating the two tokenizers is only safe if their actual normalization behavior (case
  folding, punctuation handling, stop-word removal order) genuinely matches; verify with a
  substitution+diff test before assuming they're interchangeable, not just by reading the
  constant values.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Found during a pre-release whole-branch review of `plugin/bin/lib/claim-targets/claim-targets.js`
— all three confirmed still true at this shaping pass:

- **Read-back race** (~line 400): post-write verification (#2073) re-reads immediately with no
  retry/backoff (`if (!verifyClaimLanded(deps, repoSlug, issue, opts.runId, knownTip))`). On the
  contents-API transport `knownTip` is `null`, so the read-back hits GitHub's
  eventually-consistent contents API and can legitimately return the pre-write blob — a spurious
  exit 5 on a claim that actually landed. The file's own header already warns against
  eventually-consistent GitHub reads elsewhere.
- **Claim leak on abort** (~line 227, confirmed): `abort()` releases only `claimedThisRun`
  (`releaseClaimedThisRun(deps, repoSlug, opts.runId, claimedThisRun)`). `stopOrSkip(issue,
  'unverified', 'unverified', 5, {})` runs (confirmed, ~line 401) *before* the target is pushed
  onto `claimedThisRun` (the `claimedThisRun.push(issue)` call is one line after the verification

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#1985 (unmerged, PR #2298) adds a "Drain-overlap hold" to `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`'s Auto-merge gate: before Authorization/Content judgment, `drain-pr-overlap.md`'s Step 6 checks whether this group's PR overlaps a still-open PR opened earlier by the same drain firing, and if so, explicitly **skips Authorization and Content judgment** and "fall[s] back to the normal Review Console for this group," logging:

```
AUTO {time} — Auto-merge gate: group [{issues}] held — overlaps drain PR #{pr} on {files}; merge order is a human call. Reversibility: n/a.
```

Separately, `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `needsHumanVerdict()` (the ONLY mechanism `mergeResolution()` consults to decide `leave-open` before falling through to a plain grant check) is:

```js
function needsHumanVerdict(decisions) {
  return decisionLines(decisions).find((l) => /needs-human/i.test(l) && /merge-check|assess-agent-autonomy/i.test(l)) || null;
}
```

This regex requires BOTH `needs-human` AND (`merge-check`|`assess-agent-autonomy`) on the same `decisions.md` line — a signal that only ever comes from `assess-agent-autonomy`'s Content-judgment Layer 2 (`settle-and-merge.md`, around the `2. **Content judgment**` step). Because the drain-overlap hold explicitly *skips* Content judgment, no such verdict is ever computed or logged for a drain-held group. `mergeResolution()` therefore finds no needs-human verdict, falls through to its grant check, and if every group member carries `auto:merge` or a matured `auto:merge-pending`, returns `{resolution: 'merge', reason: 'every member carries auto:merge...'}`.

Traced (not yet reproduced live): under `autonomy: unattended`, `wrap-up/review-console.md`'s Auto-resolution short-circuit invokes exactly this `console-resolve.js` merge resolution with zero human interaction. A group held back by the #1985 drain-overlap hold would reach the Review Console, and — because the hold produces no signal `needsHumanVerdict()` recognizes — the unattended auto-resolver would compute `resolution: 'merge'` and merge it anyway, silently defeating the entire purpose of the #1985 hold for exactly the operating mode (`unattended`) most likely to run a multi-group drain unattended. This is one layer downstream of the original #1480/#1596 incident #1985 was filed to prevent.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Give `console-resolve.js`'s merge-resolution path a way to recognize a live drain-overlap hold and resolve to `leave-open` for it, analogous to the existing `needs-human` carve-out — but the semantics differ: the existing carve-out (`assess-agent-autonomy` verdict) is treated as **permanent** ("authoritative all the way down," per `settle-and-merge.md`), while `drain-pr-overlap.md`'s own Step 6 hold is explicitly **not** persisted — it re-reads the overlapping PR's current state every time it runs and self-heals once that PR merges/closes. A naive regex addition that treats any historical "held — overlaps drain PR" decisions.md line as permanent would make the unattended resolver *more* conservative than #1985's own design intends. The real fix likely needs `console-resolve.js` to re-run (or receive as an already-fresh input) the same `detectCrossPRFileOverlap` check drain-pr-overlap.md's Step 6 performs, rather than trusting a historical log line — design thought needed on where that fresh state comes from at console-resolve time (a fact-pack field? a re-invocation of the check inline in resolve.js?).
- [ ] Tests: a fixture where a group's decisions.md carries a "held — overlaps drain PR" line and the overlapping PR is still open -> `mergeResolution` returns `leave-open`; the same fixture with the overlapping PR now merged/closed -> returns `merge` (assuming grants otherwise satisfy).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Under `autonomy: unattended`, a group held by #1985's drain-overlap hold is never auto-merged by `console-resolve.js` while the overlapping drain PR is still open, even when every member otherwise carries `auto:merge`.
2. Once the overlapping drain PR merges or closes, the same group's next Review Console evaluation resolves normally (no permanent lockout).
3. `npm test` green; existing `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js` cases unaffected.

## Technical Approach

Needs design thought (hence deferred): the cleanest shape is probably a new field in the run's fact pack (or `console.json`) that records the *live* drain-overlap state at Review-Console-render time, since the console's own render already runs after the Auto-merge gate would have logged the hold — the resolver could read that field instead of re-deriving from decisions.md text. Alternatively, a literal-but-honest log-line addition (e.g. `drain-overlap-hold: live` vs `drain-overlap-hold: resolved`) that `console-resolve.js` re-validates against current PR state before trusting.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — `needsHumanVerdict()`/`mergeResolution()`
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md` — Step 6, the hold's own log line
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — Auto-resolution short-circuit's carve-out list
- `tests/bin-lib/console/resolve.test.js`

## Gotchas

- Do not just make the hold's log line match the existing `needs-human`+`merge-check` regex — that would be dishonest (it isn't an `assess-agent-autonomy` verdict) and would inherit the "permanent" semantics that don't fit this hold's self-healing design.
- This gap does not affect #1944/#1984/#1985's own PR #2298 (none of the three carry `auto:merge`, so this run's own merge decision never reaches `mergeResolution()`'s grant-check branch) — it only affects a *future* group that both carries `auto:merge` and gets caught by the #1985 hold in a live unattended drain.

## Original request

Found during `/claude-tweaks:review` of #1944/#1984/#1985 (dispatch pre-build safety checks bundle, PR #2298) — self-referential review of dispatch's own merge-gating machinery surfaced this cross-cutting gap between #1985's new hold and the pre-existing unattended console auto-resolver.

**Related:** #1944, #1984, #1985

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js`'s `parseRepo` hard-codes `github.com` in its regex
(`/github\.com[:/]([^/]+)\/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/`) and is the one shared owner/repo resolver
for `bin/` CLIs (`apply-refine-labels.js`, `backlog-grant-gate.js`, `fetch-sub-issues.js`,
`file-feedback.js`, `link-records.js`, `materialize.js`, `preflight-records.js`,
`release-claim.js`, `repair-claim.js`, `resolve-blockers.js`, `resolve-linked-prs.js`, and
others). #2021 fixed the equivalent `github.com` assumption in `_shared/pr-run-comments.md`'s
`gh` calls (by resolving `{host}` from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` and passing
`--hostname {host}`), but deliberately left `parseRepo` out of scope as "a wider gap." On a
GitHub Enterprise Server remote, `parseRepo` never matches the non-`github.com` host, so every
one of its callers reports "could not resolve owner/repo" and fails outright — the class of
CLI these callers back (materialization, claim release, blocker/linked-PR resolution, refine
labeling) is used throughout this project's own pipeline, so a GHE-hosted adopter repo cannot
run `/claude-tweaks:flow`, `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`, or `/claude-tweaks:backlog` at all.

## Deliverables

- Widen `parseRepo`'s regex to capture an arbitrary host, not only `github.com` — return
  `{host, owner, repo}` instead of `{owner, repo}`, so existing callers that only destructure
  `{owner, repo}` keep working unchanged.
- Audit `parseRepo`'s callers for which ones invoke `gh` (as opposed to only using
  `{owner, repo}` in a REST/GraphQL URL path or a display string) and, for each `gh`-invoking
  call site, pass the resolved `host` through as `--hostname {host}` (mirroring #2021's fix)
  when `host` is not `github.com`. Callers that never shell out to `gh` (or that already resolve
  the host some other way) need no change beyond the destructuring above.
- Add a regression test in `tests/bin-lib/repo-resolve.test.js` (or wherever this module's
  existing tests live) asserting `parseRepo` matches an SSH and HTTPS remote on a non-`github.com`
  host and still returns the pre-existing `{owner, repo}` shape unchanged for a `github.com`
  remote.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `parseRepo('git@ghe.example.com:acme/widget.git')` and
  `parseRepo('https://ghe.example.com/acme/widget')` both return
  `{host: 'ghe.example.com', owner: 'acme', repo: 'widget'}`.
- `parseRepo('git@github.com:acme/widget.git')` still returns `{host: 'github.com', owner:
  'acme', repo: 'widget'}` — no regression on the existing, common case.
- Every existing caller of `parseRepo` that destructures only `{owner, repo}` continues to pass
  its existing test suite unmodified — the added `host` field must not break existing shapes.
- Every caller identified as `gh`-invoking during the audit above passes `--hostname {host}`
  when `host !== 'github.com'`, and a test exercises at least one such caller against a
  non-`github.com` host (a fake/injected `gh` runner, per this codebase's
  `gh-api-module-pattern` convention) to confirm the flag is actually passed.

## Technical Approach

Widen the regex in `plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js:19` to capture the host segment ahead of
`owner/repo`, e.g. `/^(?:[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+@)?([a-zA-Z0-9.-]+)[:/]([^/]+)\/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?\/?$/`
(SSH `git@{host}:{owner}/{repo}.git` and HTTPS `https://{host}/{owner}/{repo}` both match; keep
supporting the existing bare `github.com/owner/repo` shape a caller may wrap manually). Return
`{ host: m[1], owner: m[2], repo: m[3] }`. Then grep every call site in the Key Files list below
for a direct `execFileSync('gh', ...)` or `execFileSync('git', ...)` invocation that would need
`--hostname`/`GH_HOST`, per this codebase's `gh-api-module-pattern` skill (the injectable-runner
seam and `-f`/`-F`/path-placeholder conventions for `gh api` calls) — this record's scope is the
`parseRepo` widening plus that audit and the flag-threading it turns up, not a redesign of the
call sites' own logic.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/repo-resolve.js` — widen `parseRepo`'s regex and return shape
- `plugin/bin/apply-refine-labels.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/backlog-grant-gate.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/fetch-sub-issues.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/file-feedback.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/link-records.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/materialize.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/preflight-records.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/release-claim.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/repair-claim.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/resolve-blockers.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `plugin/bin/resolve-linked-prs.js` — audit for `--hostname` need
- `_shared/pr-run-comments.md` — prior-art reference only (#2021), not modified by this record

## Gotchas

- The regex must not become so permissive that it misparses a non-GitHub-shaped remote (e.g. a
  plain filesystem path or a non-forge Git host) as `{host, owner, repo}` — anchor on the
  `[host][:/]owner/repo[.git]` shape exactly as the current regex does, only generalizing the
  host segment.
- This record intentionally does not decide whether every caller needs the `host` value threaded
  through to a live `--hostname` flag — some callers may only use `{owner, repo}` for display or
  for constructing a URL where the host is irrelevant. The audit in Deliverables is scoped to
  identifying which callers actually shell out to `gh`/`git` in a way a GHE host would affect;
  don't thread `--hostname` everywhere reflexively.

## Original request

repo-resolve.js: parseRepo rejects non-github.com remotes, so every bin/ CLI fails on GitHub Enterprise

**Related:** #2021

Context: #2021 fixed the GitHub-Enterprise host resolution for `_shared/pr-run-comments.md` and `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s `gh` calls, but deliberately left `bin/lib/repo-resolve.js`'s `parseRepo` untouched — its regex (`/github\.com[:/].../`) hard-codes `github.com` and is shared by twelve `bin/` CLIs (materialize, claims, release-claim, link-records, resolve-blockers, resolve-linked-prs, and others) that derive `{owner, repo}` from the checkout's `origin` remote.

Scope: On a GHE remote, every one of those twelve callers reports "could not resolve owner/repo" and fails outright, since `parseRepo` never matches a non-github.com host. Widening the regex to accept an arbitrary host (and deciding whether callers need the host value too, not just owner/repo) touches all twelve call sites' blast radius — a documentation-level fix (#2021) should not carry that.

## Current State

Reconcile's automated hygiene sweep flags this pipeline run directory as `structurally-stuck` (`reason: no-branch`) for many consecutive passes — the cache entry for this path (`.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`, `structurally-stuck:{path}`) shows `count: 42`, `lastError: "stuck at no-branch"`, `escalated: true` — auto-filing this issue per `bin/lib/reconcile`'s escalation mechanism (#644 Deliverable 2 / #1613's visibility layer).

The stuck directory: `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413`. Its `run-state.json` **does** stamp `worktree: .claude/worktrees/dispatch-record-1413` (unlike #2228/#2230's `no-worktree` instances) and `pr: {number: 1497, url: ...}` (no `pr.branch` field). Issue #1413 is closed; `decisions.md` records the actual disposition: the record's own deliverable turned out to already be implemented and merged elsewhere (commit `0ae01b6d6`, refs #989) before this run's worktree ever branched — "a stale duplicate of an already-closed gap, not a live defect. No code change made." PR #1497 was closed without merging as a result.

**This does not match #2226's or #2228's diagnosed root causes**, and the mismatch is itself the finding worth recording: empirically re-running the exact functions `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` uses against this repo's *current* live state gives a different picture than the escalation cache's sticky `lastError`:
- `resolvePrStateByNumber(root, 1497)` (from `bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`) returns `{state: 'CLOSED', mergedAt: null, mergeCommit: null, ...}` right now — the by-number probe's `CLOSED` branch (the one #2226 found is missing a `MERGED` case) *should* be reachable and *should* match here, since this PR really is `CLOSED`, not `MERGED`.
- This run directory carries no `console.json` at all (confirmed by directory listing), so `readConsoleState(dir)` returns `'none'` — which, per the current code, routes to `skipped.push({ reason: 'console-never-rendered' })` and **never calls `trackStuckSkip`** (the function that updates `reconcile-cache.json` and drives the 7-day/3-strike escalation). A skip landing there could never accumulate a `structurally-stuck` count for `no-branch` at all going forward.

So either (a) the escalation cache's `lastError` field is stale from earlier passes and this directory has, in fact, moved to a `console-never-rendered` skip more recently (in which case it's silently stuck in a *different*, currently-untracked bucket — `console-never-rendered` has no TTL/escalation of its own), or (b) something upstream of the by-number probe (the outer `if (!branch)` gate, or an intermediate `gh` failure) is preventing the probe from ever running on the actual pass(es) that produced these 42 counts, which this investigation did not fully pin down.

## Deliverables

- Investigate directly (re-run reconcile's real archive-merged pass — dry-run flag if available — against this repo, or add temporary tracing) to determine exactly which branch of `archive-merged.js`'s logic this run dir currently lands in, rather than trusting the escalation cache's `lastError`, which this investigation found reason to doubt.
- If the finding is "stuck at `console-never-rendered` with no escalation path": that reason is deliberately excluded from `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (per the code's own comment, "each already has its own clear resolution path... that doesn't need this generic staleness backstop") — but a run dir whose PR is closed-unmerged and whose console was simply never rendered (this run stopped early on a duplicate-detection assessment, never reaching a review console) has no such path today. Decide whether `console-never-rendered` needs its own resolution route for a closed-and-abandoned (never-merged) PR specifically, distinct from the in-flight case the current exclusion is written for.
- If the finding instead confirms a genuine gap in the by-number probe itself (e.g., the outer `if (!branch)` gate not being reached the way this investigation assumed), fix that gap and land a regression test pinning it.
- Once diagnosed and fixed, resolve this specific stuck directory (`2026-08-26T155419-record-1413`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The actual current skip reason for `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413` is confirmed empirically (not assumed from the escalation cache alone).
- [ ] Whichever gap that reveals (a missing resolution path for `console-never-rendered` on a closed-unmerged PR, or a different bug in the by-number probe) is fixed, with a regression test.
- [ ] `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-08-26T155419-record-1413` is archived (or otherwise resolved) and no longer reported `structurally-stuck` by reconcile.
- [ ] The escalation cache's `lastError` staleness (if confirmed) is itself noted as a secondary finding — a `lastError` that doesn't reflect the branch a run dir currently lands in makes future triage of these auto-filed issues unreliable.

## Technical Approach

Start from `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s main sweep loop (~line 1270 onward: the `stampedWorktree`/`wtEntry`/`branch` derivation, the `#1962` by-number fallback block, `readConsoleState`, `decideArchive`) and trace this specific run dir through it step by step (or add a one-off diagnostic script that calls the same functions this investigation already called: `resolvePrStateByNumber`, `readConsoleState`, `fallbackBranch`) to find exactly where the current pass actually terminates. Cross-check against `.claude-tweaks/reconcile-cache.json`'s own `residueFailures` structure (`bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js`) to see whether other `structurally-stuck` entries show the same live-vs-cached mismatch, which would point at a systemic staleness issue in `trackResidue`/`recordResidueFailure` rather than something specific to this one run dir.

### Key Files

- `bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — the sweep loop and `#1962` fallback to trace/fix
- `bin/lib/reconcile/cache.js` — `trackResidue`/`recordResidueFailure`, if the `lastError` staleness finding needs a fix here instead
- `bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `fallbackBranch`/`branchExists`, read-only inputs to the diagnosis
- `tests/` (reconcile suite) — add the regression test for whichever gap is confirmed

## Gotchas

- This record's evidence does **not** support the same root cause as #2226 (MERGED-state gap) or #2228 (`stampedWorktree` gate gap) — do not assume either of those fixes resolves this directory without first confirming which branch this run dir actually lands in today.
- This directory has no `console.json` because the run stopped at an early duplicate-detection assessment and never reached a review console — a legitimately different lifecycle shape than a normal build-review-merge run, which may be exactly why the existing `console-never-rendered` exclusion doesn't fit it.
- The near-duplicate screen does not flag reconcile-residue records against each other by design (title-similarity excluded for `reconcile:`-prefixed titles) — the cross-references to #2226/#2228 above are a manual note, not an automated signal.
- `archiveRunDir`'s moves-first, close-last ordering must be preserved for whatever fix lands here.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file registers in `docs/skill-graph.md` only — `docs/plugin-structure.md` needs nothing.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong for a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a row there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review.
```

**Proposed:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file's `docs/skill-graph.md` edge is mandatory; a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is a judgment call, not a given.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong to apply unmodified to a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a *new dedicated row* there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case for staying out of `plugin-structure.md` entirely: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review. ```
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The Gotchas section's absolute claim that a new `_shared/*.md` file never needs a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is contradicted by #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md`, which a whole-branch review explicitly required adding to that doc's curated `_shared` row.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:specify`'s decomposition path composes each sub-issue's `## Current State` and `### Key Files` from Step 1's landscape pass (`plugin/skills/specify/decomposition-mode.md`, Step 1 item 5 — "identify existing files, schemas, APIs, and patterns that the new work will build on") and writes them in the same declarative voice whether a claim was observed in the tree or inferred from the design doc. Nothing between composition and `gh issue create` checks a current-state claim against the actual checkout. The one verification step that exists at composition time is `_shared/dependency-narration-check.md` (cited from `shaping-mode.md` only, not from the decomposition loop), and it catches a different defect: narrating another record's unmerged follow-up as landed. Shaping mode also has a one-paragraph "cheap sanity check" for human-filed defect reports that name a file, function, or error string (`plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md`, the paragraph above its Dependency-narration check subsection) — decomposition has no equivalent, and neither path distinguishes a verified observation from an assumption in the written body.

Observed cost (feedback from a private project's four-spec decomposition on plugin 6.114.0): one spec asserted a dependency subsystem was absent and would need stubbing when it was present on the branch; another justified its trigger condition with "an existing module already reads this field for these rows" when the module never read the field. Both claims were falsifiable with one grep. Both survived to build and final review respectively, where the build phase re-derived the true state and the review ledgered a write-only data gap as a follow-up record.

`spec-template.md` already has the vocabulary for the unverifiable case at a different scope: its "Empirical Premise-Check Deliverables" section handles assumptions about third-party CLI/API behavior via a blocking Task 0, and its self-check list ("No Placeholders") rejects files referenced but not defined in `Key Files`. It has no rule that a `## Current State` claim about *this repo's* existing code must carry evidence or be marked as an assumption. `/claude-tweaks:build` hands "the full spec content (including Current State, Gotchas, and acceptance criteria)" to `/superpowers:writing-plans` (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`, the writing-plans handoff) and treats every sentence as a constraint.

Related but distinct: #490 (closed) propagates *planned* sibling changes into Key Files via `crossReferenceKeyFiles`; this record is about the truth of *current-state* claims. #178 (closed wontfix) proposed a `falsified` vocabulary for brainstorming briefs, not for composed spec bodies.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Premise verification step in the decomposition loop.** In `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`'s per-sub-issue Body composition — after the body is composed, before the Ceremony and Framing calls — add a bounded verification pass over the composed `## Current State` and `### Key Files`: every claim that a named file, module, subsystem, or symbol exists or is absent, or that a named module reads/writes/calls a named field or function, gets one `git ls-files`/`git grep -n -F` probe against the checkout the decomposition runs in. Caps stated in the prose so the pass stays one step (at most 2 probes per claim, at most 12 per sub-issue — the same cap shape `challenge/SKILL.md`'s bare-`#N` evidence search uses). A confirmed claim keeps its sentence and gains an inline citation (`path:line`, or the `git ls-files` hit for existence claims). A contradicted claim is rewritten to what the tree shows before the body is filed. The pass is a content judgment applied by the model, not a new `bin/` CLI.
- [ ] **`ASSUMPTION — verify at build` marker for unverifiable claims.** A claim the probe cannot settle at decomposition time (a sibling unit's not-yet-built output, an external system, a runtime behavior no grep reaches) moves out of `## Current State`'s declarative voice into a `## Gotchas` bullet with the literal prefix `ASSUMPTION — verify at build:` followed by the claim and what would confirm it. Define the marker once in `plugin/skills/specify/spec-template.md`'s `## Gotchas` section (one template bullet showing the shape), and add one line to its "No Placeholders" self-check list: a `## Current State`/`### Key Files` sentence asserting a fact about existing code with neither an evidence citation nor the marker is incomplete.
- [ ] **Share the check with shaping mode.** Hoist the rule into a new `plugin/skills/_shared/premise-verification.md` (what to probe, the caps, the citation form, the marker), cited from both `record-creation-subissues.md`'s new step and `shaping-mode.md`'s existing "cheap sanity check" paragraph (which becomes a one-sentence pointer plus its human-filed-defect-report delta). Add the `_shared` file's row to `docs/skill-graph.md` (owned by `/specify`, the only citing skill) per CLAUDE.md's stated-once rule.
- [ ] **Build-side consumer.** In `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`'s writing-plans handoff (the "Context to provide" list), add one bullet: every `ASSUMPTION — verify at build:` bullet in the spec's `## Gotchas` is verified against the worktree before `/superpowers:writing-plans` is invoked, and its outcome (confirmed / reversed, with the probe) is logged as one `decisions.md` line per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`; a reversed assumption is surfaced in the plan's context as the corrected fact, not silently dropped.
- [ ] **Conformance test.** `tests/specify-premise-verification-prose.test.js`, sized like `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js`: pins that `record-creation-subissues.md` cites `_shared/premise-verification.md` before its Ceremony call, that `shaping-mode.md` cites it, that `spec-template.md`'s `## Gotchas` and "No Placeholders" sections both carry the literal `ASSUMPTION — verify at build` marker, and that `build/SKILL.md`'s writing-plans handoff names the marker.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/_shared/premise-verification.md` exists, states the probe forms (`git ls-files`, `git grep -n -F`), the per-claim and per-sub-issue caps, the inline citation form, and the `ASSUMPTION — verify at build:` marker; `docs/skill-graph.md` has a row for it.
2. `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md` invokes the check once per sub-issue, positioned after body composition and before the Ceremony invocation, and says a contradicted claim is rewritten before `gh issue create` / `writeRecord`.
3. `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md`'s sanity-check paragraph cites the shared file instead of restating the rule, keeping its human-filed-defect-report specific text.
4. `plugin/skills/specify/spec-template.md` shows the marker's shape under `## Gotchas` and lists the missing-evidence-or-marker case under "No Placeholders".
5. `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`'s writing-plans handoff instructs verifying every marker bullet against the worktree first and logging each outcome to `decisions.md`.
6. `node --test tests/specify-premise-verification-prose.test.js` passes, and `npm test` stays green (in particular `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js` and `tests/materiality-floor-conformance.test.js`, which pin neighbouring prose).
7. A dry decomposition of a design doc whose Current State draft asserts a file that does not exist in the tree produces a sub-issue body without that assertion (rewritten or marker-carrying), demonstrated once in the PR description with the probe output.

## Technical Approach

Prose-only change across four skill files plus one new `_shared` file and one conformance test; no `bin/` code. Mirror `_shared/dependency-narration-check.md`'s shape (what it catches, the check as a content judgment, the write-back rule) so the two composition-time checks read as siblings. Keep the probe bounded and local — the check screens, it does not verify a design; anything the caps cannot settle becomes a marker bullet rather than a deeper search. The marker is a literal string on purpose so the build-side consumer and the conformance test can match it; do not reuse any of the placeholder tokens `_shared/work-record.md`'s spec-shaped-body check rejects.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/_shared/premise-verification.md` — new: the shared rule (probes, caps, citation form, marker)
- `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md` — new premise-verification step in the per-sub-issue loop, before the Ceremony call
- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` — sanity-check paragraph becomes a pointer to the shared file plus its defect-report delta
- `plugin/skills/specify/spec-template.md` — marker shape under `## Gotchas`; new "No Placeholders" self-check line
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — writing-plans handoff: verify marker bullets first, log outcomes
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — row for the new `_shared` file
- `tests/specify-premise-verification-prose.test.js` — new conformance test

## Gotchas

- Byte-pinned conformance tests cover this prose: run `npm test` on the branch, not only the new file — `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js` asserts the cross-reference step's position relative to Snapshot invalidation, so insert the new step above the accumulation, not between the cross-reference pass and invalidation.
- The check must not trigger on citations of other records' *planned* work; that is `_shared/dependency-narration-check.md`'s domain and it already writes a `blocked-by:` edge. State the boundary in the new `_shared` file.
- Decomposition can run in a worktree whose branch is behind `main`; the probe answers for the checkout it runs in, which is the checkout the build will start from — say so, rather than probing `main`.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: none. Every Current State claim above was probed on 2026-09-09 (`shaping-mode.md` sanity-check paragraph, `record-creation-subissues.md` Body/Ceremony/Framing order, `build/SKILL.md` handoff list, `spec-template.md` sections).

## Original request

**Summary:** When `/claude-tweaks:specify` decomposes a design doc into N work-unit specs, each spec's Current State / Key Files sections state claims about sibling units and existing code as settled facts with no verification step — in one 4-spec decomposition two such premises were false and survived until build/final-review time.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** /claude-tweaks:specify (design-doc decomposition)

**Use case:**
Decomposing one design doc into four sequential work-unit specs in a private project. Two cross-unit premises were written as facts and were wrong:

1. One spec asserted a dependency subsystem was absent and would need stubbing — it was present on the branch the whole time; the build phase had to re-derive the true state before proceeding.
2. Another spec justified its trigger condition with "an existing module already reads this field for these rows" — the module never read the field at all; the final review found the produced data was write-only, and the gap had to be ledgered as a follow-up record.

Both claims were falsifiable with a grep in seconds. The gap: decomposition has no premise-verification step, and the spec format gives a verified observation and an unverified assumption the same voice, so downstream phases inherit errors as constraints.

Suggested directions: (a) verify each cross-unit/current-state claim against the actual tree at decomposition time (the same discipline the spec-research phase applies to UI claims) and cite the evidence; or (b) mark unverifiable claims explicitly as `ASSUMPTION — verify at build`, so the build phase treats them as inputs to check rather than facts to build on. Related but distinct from #490 (cross-referencing forward-declared sibling changes): this is about the truth of current-state claims, not the propagation of planned ones.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.0

Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-start.js` walks `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` twice per session start. The stale-runs report pulls up to `MAX_REPORTED` entries from `context.js`'s `iterRunDirsWithState(ctx.cwd)`, which anchors to the main checkout, sorts newest-first, reads each `run-state.json`, skips `status: 'clean'` runs, and skips runs whose `archive/{name}` twin is `clean` or freshly `archiving`. The #1493 AC5 staged-proposals scan, a few lines below, needs the opposite status filter (only `clean` runs, name-matched to `-(tidy|sweep)-standalone`, with a non-empty `staged/`) and therefore re-implements the walk by hand: its own `mainCheckoutRoot` anchor, its own `readdirSync` + name filter + sort + reverse, its own `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(run-state.json))` per dir, and its own early-break at `MAX_REPORTED`. Its comment says why: the iterator "deliberately excludes status `clean` runs … so it needs its own directory read". The hand-rolled copy also lacks the iterator's archive-twin and `archiving`-claim skips, so a clean standalone run whose archival is mid-flight can still be listed. Both blocks then build the same advisory shape by hand: `- {name} — {detail}` lines, a header sentence, and the #803 relay trailer.

`bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`'s `iterCleanRunDirs` (#1733) is a third copy of the same clean-only walk, without the anchor and without the twin skips.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `iterRunDirsWithState(cwd, { status } = {})` in `context.js`: an optional `status` filter — `'clean'` yields only clean runs, absent keeps today's exclude-clean behavior byte-for-byte — applied at the one existing status check so the anchor, ordering, archive-twin skip, and `archiving`-claim skip are shared by both shapes. `listRunDirsWithState`/`listRunDirs` pass the option through unchanged in their default form.
- [ ] `session-start.js`'s staged-proposals scan becomes a `for … of iterRunDirsWithState(ctx.cwd, { status: 'clean' })` loop that keeps only its own two concerns: the `-(tidy|sweep)-standalone` name test on `path.basename(dir)` and the non-empty `staged/` read, with the existing `MAX_REPORTED` early break. The hand-rolled `readdirSync`/sort/`run-state.json` read is deleted.
- [ ] One `advisoryBanner(header, lines, trailer)` helper in `session-start.js` used by both the stale-runs and staged-proposals blocks, producing byte-identical strings to today's inline concatenation (the tests below are the proof).
- [ ] `archive-merged.js`'s `iterCleanRunDirs(root)` reduced to `[...iterRunDirsWithState(root, { status: 'clean' })]`, so the third copy disappears; its callers and the `{ dir, state }` shape are unchanged.
- [ ] Tests: `tests/hooks-context.test.js` cases for the option (default excludes clean; `{ status: 'clean' }` yields only clean; both shapes honor the archive-twin skip); the existing #1493/#1494 cases in `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` pass unmodified; one new session-start case that a clean `-tidy-standalone` run with a `clean` archive twin is not listed (the skip the hand-rolled walk lacked).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `session-start.js` contains no `fs.readdirSync` of the pipelines directory and no direct `run-state.json` parse; both advisory scans iterate `iterRunDirsWithState`.
2. With no option, `iterRunDirsWithState` yields exactly what it yields today for every existing fixture (the `hooks-context`, `session-start`, `archive-merged`, `console-execute`, and residue-probe suites are the proof).

Surface: infra

## Current State
Three functions in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` carry the same directory-staleness stanza: `let mtimeMs; try { mtimeMs = fs.statSync(dir).mtimeMs; } catch { return false; } return (now - mtimeMs) > TTL;` — `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded` against `ADHOC_SUPERSEDED_TTL_MS` (30d), `isOrphanedMint` against `ORPHAN_MINT_TTL_MS` (24h), and `isStructurallyStuck` against `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_TTL_MS` (7d). Each takes `now = Date.now()` as its last parameter and treats an unstat-able directory as not stale (fail toward "keep"). The copies are byte-for-byte the same logic, so a change to the staleness basis (ctime instead of mtime, tolerating clock skew, treating `ENOENT` differently from `EACCES`) has to be made three times, and `isAbandonedInterrupted`, which uses the events log rather than the stat, is the reminder that a fourth copy would be the path of least resistance for the next detector. The related consolidation records (#1732 classifier, #1733 loop extraction) both build on this primitive existing first.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `isStaleDir(dir, ttlMs, now = Date.now())` in `archive-merged.js`: the one stat-and-compare, returning `false` on any stat failure, `true` iff `(now - mtimeMs) > ttlMs`; exported alongside the existing predicates.
- [ ] `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded`, `isOrphanedMint`, and `isStructurallyStuck` each reduce to their own guard clauses plus one `isStaleDir(dir, <their constant>, now)` call; their signatures, exports, and `now` defaults unchanged.
- [ ] Unit tests for the primitive in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` beside the existing `fs.utimesSync`-backdated fixtures: stale past TTL → `true`; exactly at TTL → `false` (strict `>` preserved); fresh → `false`; missing directory → `false`.
- [ ] The three predicates' existing cases stay green unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `archive-merged.js` contains exactly one `fs.statSync(...).mtimeMs` expression, inside `isStaleDir`.
2. The three predicates call `isStaleDir` with their own TTL constant; the constants' names and values are unchanged and still exported.
3. `isStaleDir` is exported and has its own test cases for the four outcomes above, including the boundary (`now - mtimeMs === ttlMs` is not stale).
4. All existing cases in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` pass without modification; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
A mechanical extraction: the stanza's only free variables are `dir`, the TTL constant, and `now`. Keep the comparison strict (`>`) and the catch-to-`false` posture identical; both are load-bearing (`isStructurallyStuck`'s comment: "pure except for the one mtime stat", and the orphan-mint comment's fail-toward-keep rationale). Land first among the four `archive-merged.js` records: #1732's classifier calls this helper, and #1733/#1737 are independent of it but touch the same file, so sequence, never parallel.

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded`, `isOrphanedMint`, `isStructurallyStuck`, `module.exports`.

## Gotchas

- `isAbandonedInterrupted` is not a stat-based detector (events-log recency); do not force it onto `isStaleDir`.
- Do not change the fail-closed direction: an unreadable directory is "not stale" everywhere today, and `archiveMerged()` relies on that to leave a permission-broken run dir alone.

## Current State
`isStructurallyStuck` (~line 664, `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`) reimplements the identical "fs.statSync(dir).mtimeMs, catch->false, compare (now-mtimeMs) > TTL" stanza already present in `isAdHocStandaloneSuperseded` (~line 85) and `isOrphanedMint` (~line 97), each against its own TTL constant.

## Deliverables

Surface: infra

## Current State
`archiveMerged()` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` ends with two loops that run the same merged-PR archive sequence: the main loop over `iterRunDirsWithState(root)` and the #1544 clean-status sweep over `iterCleanRunDirs(root)`. Both do `resolvePrState(root, branch)` → `readConsoleState(dir)` → `decideArchive(prState, consoleState)` → skip on `decision.action === 'skip'` → `localHasMerge(root, prState.mergeCommit)` with the `local-behind-merge` / `merge-commit-unknown` skip reasons → `dryRun` short-circuit → `archiveRunDir(root, dir)` → `trackArchiveResult(root, repoSlug, dir, result)` → push to `archived`/`skipped`. The copies already differ in one place that the duplication hides: the main loop's `decideArchive` skip also calls `trackStuckSkip(root, repoSlug, dir, decision.reason)` (#1613's structurally-stuck visibility), the clean loop's does not.

The two loops need different inputs only at the front: the main loop derives `branch` from the worktree list (with the structurally-stuck skip on `no-worktree`/`no-branch`), the clean loop from `fallbackBranch(root, dir, state)` because a `clean` run's `state.worktree` is null by construction. `iterCleanRunDirs` exists because `iterRunDirsWithState` in `bin/lib/hooks/context.js` skips `status: 'clean'` by design, and that generator has eight callers (hooks dispatcher, session-start, console-execute, the residue probe, the stray-run-dir sweep, reconcile's index) that all rely on the exclusion.

## Deliverables
- [ ] One helper in `archive-merged.js`, `archiveMergedRun({ root, repoSlug, dir, branch, dryRun, onSkip })` → `{ outcome: 'archived' | 'skipped', reason? }`, holding the full sequence from `resolvePrState` through `trackArchiveResult`; `onSkip(reason)` is the hook the main loop uses to call `trackStuckSkip` on a `decideArchive` skip, so the one existing difference becomes an explicit parameter rather than a divergence.
- [ ] Both loops call the helper: the main loop after its worktree-derived `branch` and structurally-stuck handling, the clean loop after `fallbackBranch`; each keeps only its branch derivation and its `archived`/`skipped` push.
- [ ] `iterRunDirsWithState`'s contract is unchanged and `iterCleanRunDirs` stays as the clean-status enumerator; the record's alternative (a state-tagged tuple from the shared iterator) is declined — see Technical Approach.
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`: existing cases unmodified and green; one new case that a clean-status run whose `decideArchive` skips reports the skip reason without invoking `trackStuckSkip` (pins the `onSkip` asymmetry as intended, so a later reader does not "fix" it), and one that a main-loop skip still does.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `archive-merged.js` contains exactly one call site each for `resolvePrState`, `decideArchive`, `localHasMerge`, and `archiveRunDir` inside `archiveMerged()`'s merged-PR path (the helper); neither loop body calls them directly.
2. For every existing fixture, `archiveMerged({ dryRun: true })` returns the same `archived`/`skipped` sets as before the change.
3. `iterRunDirsWithState` in `bin/lib/hooks/context.js` is byte-identical; no other caller changes.
4. The `trackStuckSkip`-on-main-loop-only behavior is preserved and pinned by a test.
5. `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Share the sequence at the caller, not the iterator. Widening `iterRunDirsWithState` to yield `clean` runs behind a tag would touch a generator that every hook invocation drives (`context.js`'s own comment: it "drives both the fallback event-attribution scan and every reconcile check's enumeration") and force each of its other callers to filter the new tuple, for a benefit that is entirely local to `archiveMerged()`. The helper is a pure extraction: move the shared block into a function whose only free variables are the ones both loops already have in scope. Land this before #1732 where possible — #1732's per-kind action switch then dispatches the `merged` kind straight to this helper instead of inlining the sequence a third time. Same file as #1732, #1734, #1737: sequence, never build in parallel.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `archiveMerged` (both loops), `iterCleanRunDirs`, `decideArchive`, `localHasMerge`, `archiveRunDir`, `trackArchiveResult`, `trackStuckSkip`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — `iterRunDirsWithState` (read for the contract; unchanged).
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `fallbackBranch` (clean loop's branch source; unchanged).
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — the #1544 clean-status fixture (around the `status: 'clean', worktree: null, pr: { branch: … }` case) is the template for the new pins.

## Gotchas
- `resolvePrState` (imported from `pr-state.js`) reads the reconcile PR cache; keep it inside the helper so a future change to its caching cannot land in one loop only.
- The clean loop's comment block (#1544 rationale: why `state.worktree` is null and why `fallbackBranch` is the right source) must stay on the clean loop, not move into the helper — it explains the input, not the sequence.

## Current State
