Surface: backend

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js`'s `mergedEvidence()` passes a caller-derived ref name as a bare positional argument to git at two call sites:

- `runGit(['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', branch, integration], root)`
- `runGit(['cherry', integration, branch], root)`

This repo's `gh-api-module-pattern` skill states the rule directly: a caller-supplied value beginning with `-` is still read as an option, and for `git` the separator is `--end-of-options`, not `--` (`--` only guards the pathspec argument slot, a different position). `docs/incident-log.md` carries the same rule for `rev-parse`/`merge-base`.

Record #1463 added a third call in the same file (`hasCommitSinceRunStart`'s `git log`) and adopted `--end-of-options` there, per CLAUDE.md's "adopt new conventions in new code first, then migrate existing ones deliberately". These two call sites are the deliberate migration that convention-adoption implies.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `mergedEvidence()`'s `merge-base --is-ancestor` call places `--end-of-options` before the two ref arguments.
- [ ] `mergedEvidence()`'s `git cherry` call does the same.
- [ ] No behavior change for any ref name git can actually produce — the existing `tests/run-integrity.test.js` AC1/AC2/AC3a cases stay green unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both call sites in `mergedEvidence()` pass their ref arguments after an `--end-of-options` separator.
2. `node --test tests/run-integrity.test.js` passes with no test edits required.
3. `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach
Two argument-array edits, no logic change: insert `'--end-of-options'` immediately before the first ref argument in each call — `['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', '--end-of-options', branch, integration]` and `['cherry', '--end-of-options', integration, branch]`. `hasCommitSinceRunStart`'s `git log` call in the same file is the in-file model (it already places `--end-of-options` before `branch`, followed by `--` for the pathspec slot); `git cherry` takes no pathspec, so no trailing `--` there.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/run-integrity.js` — `mergedEvidence()` (the `merge-base --is-ancestor` and `cherry` calls), `hasCommitSinceRunStart()` (existing `--end-of-options` example).

Surface: infra

## Current State
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` keeps four session-scoped exclusion files, each with its own shape, producer, reader, and report:

| File | Shape | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dispatch-blocked-excluded.json` | `{number, blockedBy: number[]}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (removed from the pool) | `blocked-exclusion-report.md` |
| `dispatch-open-pr-excluded.json` | `{number, pr}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (removed from the pool) | `open-pr-exclusion-report.md`; SKILL.md's `#N` / `#N,#M` forms (reason lookup, #1973) |
| `dispatch-oversized-excluded.json` | `{records: number[], size, threshold}[]` | `queue-pull-script.md` (stays in the pool) | `next-ranking.md` (excludes), `oversized-group-report.md` |
| `dispatch-firing-excluded.json` | `number[]` | SKILL.md's Loop per `firing-exclusion.md` (append per iteration) | `next-ranking.md` (excludes) |

Every one is read with an inline `fs.existsSync(p) ? require(p) : []` and filtered with hand-written `Set` logic inside a `node -e` block embedded in the skill's markdown; `next-ranking.md`'s bash block alone carries two different key derivations (`keyOf(g)` for oversized record-sets, member membership for firing numbers). The next exclusion reason (a residue class, a maintainer deny-list, a freshness veto) copies the pattern a fifth time or forces this refactor later. No `bin/` module owns the concept: `bin/lib/dispatch/` holds `artifact-verdict.js`, `ceremony-derive.js`, `queue-order.js` only.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js`: one module owning the shape and the file — `readExclusions(path)` → `{ reason, records: number[], detail }[]` (absent/unreadable → `[]`), `appendExclusion(path, entry)`, `excludedNumbers(entries, reasons)` → `Set<number>`, and `groupIsExcluded(group, entries, reasons)` (true when any member is in the set, the semantics `firing-exclusion.md` and `next-ranking.md` already use), with unit tests in `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/exclusions.test.js`.
- [ ] One session-scoped `dispatch-exclusions.json` replacing the four files: `queue-pull-script.md` writes `blocked` (`detail: { blockedBy }`), `open-pr` (`detail: { pr }`), and `oversized` (`detail: { size, threshold }`) entries through `appendExclusion` after truncating the file at the start of its run; SKILL.md's Loop appends `firing` entries through the same call per `firing-exclusion.md`'s rule (unchanged trigger conditions).
- [ ] `next-ranking.md`'s script filters with `groupIsExcluded(g, entries, ['oversized', 'firing'])` — one derivation, no `keyOf` vs member split; the `#N` / `#N,#M` reason lookup reads `open-pr` entries from the same file.
- [ ] The three report files and `blocked-exclusion-report.md` read the one file filtered by reason, rendering byte-identical lines to today; `firing-exclusion.md` and `dispatch/SKILL.md` name the new file and the reason vocabulary.
- [ ] `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` (which extracts and executes `next-ranking.md`'s bash block) updated to seed `dispatch-exclusions.json` entries instead of two files; `tests/session-tmp-root-migration.test.js` and `tests/node-e-snippet-syntax.test.js` stay green (they scan the same blocks).
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md` gains the new module wherever it lists `bin/lib/{name}/` modules (it names the directory convention, not each file, today — add a line only if a per-module list exists); `_shared/session-tmp-root.md` enumerates no dispatch file names, so it needs no edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Exactly one session-scoped exclusion file is written or read anywhere under `plugin/skills/dispatch/`; `grep -rn "excluded.json" plugin/skills` returns no match.
2. All four reasons survive with their current pool semantics: `blocked` and `open-pr` still remove candidates from `dispatch-groups.json` in the queue pull; `oversized` and `firing` still leave groups in the pool and are excluded only by the ranking script.
3. Each report renders the same line text as before for the same inputs; the `#N` form still names the linked PR for an `open-pr` exclusion.
4. `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`'s four scenarios (absent file, one excluded group, all excluded → `null`, bundle-member match) pass against the new shape; `exclusions.js` has its own unit coverage; `npm test` is green.
5. Adding a fifth reason requires one `appendExclusion` call site and one report, no new file or filter logic — demonstrated by a test that seeds an unknown reason and shows the ranking ignores it while `readExclusions` returns it.

## Technical Approach
Move the concept into code and leave the skills as callers: the markdown scripts already shell out to `node -e` with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/...` requires, so `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/dispatch/exclusions.js')` inside those blocks is the same pattern `session-tmp.js` is loaded with today. One file rather than one-per-reason: the readers already differ only by reason, and a single array with a `reason` field is what makes the fifth reason a one-line append. Keep the pool split (`blocked`/`open-pr` removed at queue pull; `oversized`/`firing` filtered at ranking) exactly as is — the record is about the file mechanism, not the exclusion semantics.

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/queue-pull-script.md` — the `files` map and the three producer writes.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/next-ranking.md` — the `files` map, the `firingExcluded`/`oversizedKeys` filter.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/firing-exclusion.md` — the append rule.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md` — Loop paragraph; `#N` / `#N,#M` bullets (#1973 reason lookup).
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/blocked-exclusion-report.md`, `open-pr-exclusion-report.md`, `oversized-group-report.md` — readers.
- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/` — new `exclusions.js` beside `queue-order.js`.
- `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/` — script-executing test and new unit test.

## Gotchas
- `dispatch-blocked-excluded-body.json` is an intermediate of the body-text blocker pass, not an exclusion list; leave it alone.
- The reports' "drain + zero-eligible silence" exception keys on report content, not file presence; reading one file for all reasons must not change when a report is omitted.
- `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` extracts the bash block by a fenced-code regex; keep the block's fence and the `eval "$(node -e …)"` prologue shape so the extraction still matches.
- Truncate-then-append in the queue pull must happen once at the start of `queue-pull-script.md`, before the blocked pass — the firing entries appended by the Loop live in the same file and must survive the per-iteration re-pull, so the truncation drops only non-`firing` entries (`readExclusions` → filter → rewrite), never the whole file.

## Original request

Whole-branch pre-release review finding (v6.113.0 -> origin/main, d68ffa7d9..7036ce768): the next exclusion reason will either copy this one-off pattern a fifth time or require a larger later refactor to unify what should have been one mechanism from the start.

#647's expand phase shipped per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` (`permittedGrants`), fixing a bug where the flat top-level `reason` string could pair a granted `bornReady` with the other grant's denial text. Two skill-text consumers carry a matching read-side fallback, tagged with the same removal condition: `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (line ~144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (line ~223), both doing `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }`.

Confirmed at shaping time (2026-08-17): the module header text, both fallback call sites, and `skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line (`↳ trust: {provenance} / {band} — {verdict}{, {coverage}% coverage}`) all reproduce exactly as described — the trust-table snippet's `bornReady`/`reason` output fields (written to `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) are genuinely dead: nothing downstream reads or renders them.

The removal date (2026-11-16) has **not** yet passed as of this record's shaping (2026-08-17) — it is roughly three months out. This record documents and prepares the contract phase; it does not authorize building the removal before that date.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Verify, at build time, that the current date is on or after 2026-11-16 (the first release on/after that date) before making any of the changes below. If built before that date, stop without editing anything and report the record as not yet actionable — see Acceptance Criteria #1, a hard gate.
- [ ] Re-run `grep -rn "permittedGrants" skills/ bin/` to confirm every consumer still reads only `grants.*` shapes (no new flat-key consumer introduced since shaping).
- [ ] Remove the flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys from `permittedGrants`'s return value in `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`, and delete the module-header comment block documenting the now-resolved removal condition.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/capture/SKILL.md` (the `(permitted.grants || {}).bornReady || { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` pattern and its explanatory comment), reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly.
- [ ] Remove the matching read-side fallback in `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (same pattern, same treatment).
- [ ] Drop the dead `bornReady`/`reason` output fields from `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet (the `node -e` block that writes `/tmp/backlog-refine-trust.json`) — confirmed nothing downstream (`skills/backlog/refine-lanes.md`'s rendered trust-consequence line) reads them.
- [ ] Decide, and record the decision inline as a code/skill-text comment, how to handle the two disclosed conflation residues before deleting the flat keys:
  1. Withheld grants share one reason string today — `grants.bornAuthorized.reason` can carry born-ready's rationale on the human-filed path. Decide whether this stays as-is (the per-grant shape already fixes the *granted*-path pairing bug; the withheld-grant sharing is a separate, lower-severity residue) or gets its own follow-up record.
  2. The granted path's flat `reason` today carries positive rationale text ("class is clean, ceiling is unattended, grant origination opted in") that no per-grant key reproduces. Decide whether to populate that positive rationale into the granted per-grant `reason` field, or record explicitly (in a code comment) that it is intentionally dropped as noise once the grant itself is visible via `granted: true`.
- [ ] Update or remove the flat-key compat tests in the `bin-lib/issues` test suite to match the per-grant-only shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hard precondition, checked first:** the build only proceeds once the current date is on or after 2026-11-16. A build attempted before that date stops without modifying any file and reports the record as not yet actionable — this is not a normal "build failed" outcome, it is the record's own documented gate.
2. `permittedGrants` (`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`) returns only the per-grant `grants.{bornReady,bornAuthorized}.{granted,reason}` shape — no flat `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized`/`reason` keys at the top level.

4. `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table snippet no longer computes or emits `bornReady`/`reason` fields.
5. The two conflation-residue decisions are recorded (as a comment near the code they affect, or in this record's own close-out note) — not silently dropped.
6. `npm test` passes with the flat-key compat tests updated or removed.

## Technical Approach

Start with the grep re-verification (Deliverables item 2) — the module header itself calls this out as the first step, since a consumer could have appeared between #647 shipping and this record's execution.

`bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`: delete the flat keys from `permittedGrants`'s two return objects (denied-path and granted-path, around current lines 128-155) and the header comment block (lines 10-15) documenting the removal condition — the condition is satisfied, not evergreen.

`skills/capture/SKILL.md` (~line 144) and `skills/backlog/refine-mode.md` (~line 223): drop the `|| { granted: permitted.bornReady, reason: permitted.reason }` fallback half of each destructure, reading `permitted.grants.bornReady` directly; delete the accompanying "older installed build" comment.

`skills/backlog/refine-mode.md`'s trust-table `node -e` block (~lines 219-234): remove `bornReady`/`reason` from the `out[issue.number]` object literal.

Fold the two conflation-residue decisions into the same edit pass — they're small text/comment changes, not separate work.

Grep the `bin-lib/issues` test directory for `bornReady`/`bornAuthorized` flat-key assertions on `permittedGrants`'s return value and update/remove them alongside the source change, in the same commit.

## Gotchas

- **Date gate is load-bearing, not advisory.** This record was shaped on 2026-08-17, roughly three months before the 2026-11-16 backstop. Confirmed by reading `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s own module header, which states the removal condition explicitly and cites `policy-deprecations.md`'s dated-backstop shape as precedent for this pattern (see also #628/#629, which apply the same shape to `policy.yml` key retirements). - **Information loss is real if the conflation residues are skipped.** Deleting the flat keys without deciding the two residues (the Deliverables item above them) silently drops the granted-path's positive rationale text — no per-grant key reproduces it today. This isn't a formatting nit; a human reading a future trust/grant explanation loses the "why" for a clean grant unless this is deliberately decided and recorded.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`fileMatchesFrontendPredicate` (`plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/index.js`, the Layer 3 sniff) returns true when a file's extension is in `TRIGGER_EXTENSIONS` or when any path segment is in `TRIGGER_PATH_SEGMENTS = ['components', 'pages', 'app', 'routes', 'views', 'ui']`. The segment rule exists so app-router `page.ts`/`layout.ts` files without a rendering extension are still caught. It has no exclusion, so Next.js API route handlers — `app/api/**/route.{ts,js}` (app router) and `pages/api/**` (pages router) — match on the `app`/`pages` segment even though they render nothing. `skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md`'s Match rule (two positive clauses, no exclusion) and its Negative cases list (which names `.ts`/`.js` "outside any trigger path" only) describe the same behavior, so the sniff and its documentation agree with each other and are both wrong for this case.

Observed on plugin 6.114.0: a record whose diff was two `app/api/**/route.ts` handlers, one vitest file, and four markdown files, with no `Surface:` header (filed before that field existed, so Layer 2 could not rule), returned `{"decision":"proceed","track":"web"}` from `design-detect.js` in `review`, `polish`, and `survey` modes. The run overrode the verdict by hand three times, each logged as a deviation, while `/build`'s own design pre-build step on the same run had already been skipped as "no frontend surface". Layer 3 is a fallback that runs only when nothing was declared (`layer3Applies`), so the false positive costs exactly the records that most need the sniff to be right.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` (245 lines) covers "trigger path segments match regardless of extension" and the zero-match skip; no case exercises an API route path.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add an API-route exclusion to `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate`: after the extension check (a `.tsx` under `app/api/` still matches on extension) and before the segment scan, return false when the normalized path contains `app/api/` or `pages/api/` as adjacent segments (`(^|/)(app|pages)/api/`), so the `app`/`pages` segment rule never fires for a Next.js API route. Keep `TRIGGER_PATH_SEGMENTS` unchanged; the exclusion is a named constant (`API_ROUTE_SEGMENTS` or a regex) with a comment citing this record and the two Next.js conventions.
- [ ] `frontend-detection.md`: add a third clause to the Match rule stating the exclusion (segment matches under `app/api/` or `pages/api/` do not count; extension matches still do), and add "Next.js API route handlers — `app/api/**/route.{ts,js}`, `pages/api/**`" to the Negative cases list, so the sniff and its documentation agree.
- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js`: `app/api/users/route.ts` and `pages/api/health.ts` do not match; `src/app/api/x/route.js` does not match; `app/api/x/page.tsx` still matches (extension wins); `app/dashboard/page.ts` still matches (segment rule intact); `layer3` over the observed file list (two `app/api/**/route.ts`, one `.test.ts`, four `.md`) returns the sniff skip.
- [ ] `docs/incident-log.md` / `CLAUDE.md` untouched; if `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s `design-detect` line enumerates the trigger tables, leave it — the tables themselves did not change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate('app/api/users/route.ts')`, `('pages/api/health.ts')`, and `('src/app/api/x/route.js')` return false; `('app/api/x/page.tsx')` and `('app/dashboard/page.ts')` return true.
2. `layer3([...two app/api route.ts, one .test.ts, four .md])` returns `{ proceed: false, reason: SKIP_REASONS.NON_FRONTEND_SNIFF }`; `node bin/design-detect.js --mode review` over the same list returns a skip decision, not `proceed`.
3. Every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` and `cli.test.js` passes unchanged.
4. `frontend-detection.md`'s Match rule has the exclusion clause and its Negative cases list names Next.js API route handlers with both path shapes.
5. `npm test` green.

## Technical Approach

One predicate change, no new layer: the exclusion is scoped to the two Next.js API conventions the report observed, applied only to the segment rule so the extension rule keeps precedence. Do not generalise to `routes/` (SvelteKit `+server.ts`, Remix resource routes) in this record — those are a different convention with a different marker and belong in a follow-up if observed; name that boundary in the code comment.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/design-detect/index.js` — exclusion constant + check in `fileMatchesFrontendPredicate`, above the segment scan
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md` — Match rule clause 3; Negative cases bullet
- `tests/bin-lib/design-detect/index.test.js` — the cases in Deliverables

## Gotchas

- Normalize backslashes before matching (the function already does); the exclusion regex must run on the normalized string so Windows paths behave.
- `pages/api/` under a `src/` prefix and `app/api/` nested inside a monorepo package path (`packages/web/app/api/...`) must both be excluded; anchor on the adjacent segment pair, not on path start.
- A `.tsx` under `app/api/` is exotic but possible (a handler that renders an OG image with JSX); the extension rule keeps it frontend on purpose, and the test pins that.
- `frontend-detection.md`'s trigger tables are cited as "web-only" by the native track's routing paragraph; the exclusion does not change that property, so no native-track text needs editing.

## Original request

**Summary:** `design-detect.js`'s Layer 3 path sniff marks Next.js app-router API route handlers (`app/api/**/route.ts`) as frontend, so a backend-only record without a `Surface:` header returns `proceed` for review, polish and survey.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/lib/design-detect (Layer 3 file-extension / path-segment sniff) and skills/design-wrapper/frontend-detection.md

**Use case:**
Layer 3's trigger-path table treats any file under a `/app/` segment as frontend so that app-router `page.ts`/`layout.ts` files without a `.tsx` extension are still caught. That rule also matches `app/api/**/route.ts` — Next.js app-router API route handlers, which render nothing. On a record whose diff was two Next.js API route handler files (`app/api/**/route.ts`) plus a vitest file and four markdown files, with no `Surface:` header (a code-health-filed record predating that field), `design-detect.js --mode review`, `--mode polish` and `--mode survey` all returned `{"decision":"proceed","track":"web"}`. The caller then either pays for Impeccable critique/audit over request handlers, or overrides the CLI's verdict by hand — which is what the run did, three times, each as a logged deviation — while `/build`'s own design pre-build step on the same run had already been skipped for "no frontend surface, two backend API route files".

Suggested change: exclude `**/app/api/**/route.{ts,js}` (and `pages/api/**`) from the `/app/` and `/pages/` path triggers, or require a rendering extension when the only match is a path segment and the file is a `route.ts`; add "Next.js API route handlers" to `frontend-detection.md`'s Negative cases list so the sniff and its documentation agree.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.114.0

stage the way `build`/`review`/`wrap-up` are.

Add three entries to the existing `NESTED_PARENT` object literal in
`plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` (~line 21), each `'enclosing'` — the identical value every

remove the three names from `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js`'s `ALLOWLIST` and add

nine entries' own coverage already uses.

- `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` — add three entries to `NESTED_PARENT` (~line 21)
- `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js` — remove the three names from `ALLOWLIST`
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js` (or the actual location of `NESTED_PARENT`'s existing
  test coverage — verify at build time) — add coverage for the three new entries

## Gotchas

- This record resolves the phase-attribution question itself (all three nest) rather than

Surface: infra

## Current State

`agent-browser` is a third-party tool this plugin depends on optionally (CLAUDE.md's Dependencies
table) — it is not part of this repo's own codebase; `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md`
documents its usage but does not own its implementation. That reference file's documented operation
vocabulary (open, snapshot, find, click, fill, screenshot, vitals, trace, etc.) has no
color-scheme/emulation flag.

Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by
`prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML
fixture with the target CSS rules copied in and the desired scheme's token values inlined, opened
via `file://`, instead of driving the live app in the actual scheme under test — a real but
indirect substitute.

Because `agent-browser` is external, this record's scope is bounded by what this repo can
actually change: whether the tool already supports color-scheme emulation through some mechanism
not yet documented here, and if not, formalizing the documented workaround so a future verifier
doesn't have to rediscover it.

## Deliverables

- Investigate whether the installed `agent-browser` version already supports color-scheme
  emulation via an undocumented flag, environment variable, or underlying CDP passthrough (e.g.
  `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`) — check its own `--help` output and any bundled documentation
  first.
- If a mechanism already exists: document it in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s operation
  vocabulary, with a usage example.
- If no mechanism exists: document the standalone-HTML-fixture workaround (build a minimal
  fixture with the target CSS and the desired scheme's token values inlined, open via `file://`)
  as the recommended pattern in `agent-browser-reference.md`, so a future verifier facing the same
  gap has a documented path instead of reinventing it — and, separately, file feedback against
  `agent-browser` itself (outside this repo) requesting the capability, since this repo cannot add
  a feature to a tool it doesn't own.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `agent-browser-reference.md` documents either (a) a working color-scheme emulation flag/option,
  verified against the actually-installed tool version, or (b) the standalone-fixture workaround
  pattern, clearly labeled as a workaround rather than a native capability.
- Whichever path is documented is validated by actually using it to verify a light-mode-only (or
  dark-mode-only) CSS change against a real project with `prefers-color-scheme`-only theming —
  not merely described in the abstract.
- If no native mechanism exists, upstream feedback is filed against `agent-browser` (outside this
  repo's own issue tracker) requesting the capability, and that filing is referenced from this
  record's closing comment.

## Technical Approach

Run `agent-browser --help` (and any subcommand-specific help, e.g. `agent-browser open --help`)
against the actually-installed version to check for an existing but undocumented emulation
option before assuming none exists — third-party tools frequently expose CDP-passthrough flags
that aren't surfaced in every doc surface. If nothing surfaces, formalize the fixture-based
workaround already used as a real substitute: a minimal standalone HTML file with the target
CSS rules and the desired scheme's computed token values inlined, opened via `agent-browser open
file://<path>`. Document whichever path is real in `agent-browser-reference.md`'s existing
operation-vocabulary section, in the same format as its other documented operations.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/browse/agent-browser-reference.md` — document the flag (if found) or the
  fixture-workaround pattern (if not)

## Gotchas

- `agent-browser` is a third-party dependency, not part of this repo's own codebase — this
  record cannot add a capability to the tool itself; it can only document what already exists or
  formalize a workaround, plus file upstream feedback if the capability is genuinely absent.
- Don't document a workaround as if it were a native capability — the Acceptance Criteria
  requires the documentation to be honest about which case applies.

## Original request

**Summary:** Verifying a light-mode-only CSS change in a project whose theming is driven solely by `prefers-color-scheme` media queries (no in-app toggle) required building a standalone HTML fixture instead of driving the live app, because agent-browser's documented operation vocabulary has no color-scheme/emulation flag.

**Kind:** Gap
